perf.summary: Reuse the gcd's Bezout coefficient instead of computing a second ModInverse from scratch.
perf.currentCost: Run computes Gcd(a,m) via a plain Euclid loop, then ModInverse(a_,m_) runs ExtGcd AGAIN over essentially the same numbers — two full Euclid descents where one suffices.
perf.proposedChange: Call ExtGcd(a, m, out x, out y) once to get g and the coefficient x; then if b%g==0 set result = ( (x % m_) * (b/g) ) % m_, normalized positive. This fuses the gcd computation and the inverse into a single Euclid pass.
perf.rationale: Halves the Euclidean work (one descent instead of two) and removes a redundant division chain. Same x.
perf.risk: Must reduce x modulo m_ (= m/g) since ExtGcd gives the inverse of a modulo m, and a_*x ≡ g (mod m) implies x is inverse of a_ mod m_. Normalize x to [0,m_) before multiplying. Verify sign normalization matches the existing `if (x<0) x += m_` path.
